title: APX2 Induction via Herbicide Infiltration
author: Diep R R Ganguly
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.riid4ce
materials: Make fresh herbicide solutions (dissolve in ethanol): 50 mg DBMIB in 15 mL ethanol = 10 mM 20 mg DCMU in 40 mL ethanol = 2 mM 26 mg MV in 40 mL ethanol = 2.5 µM Control = ethanol only.

steps.title: Grow plants under low light
steps.instruction: Grow plants under low‑moderate light conditions measured at 60–100 µM (ensure light intensity is recorded).

steps.title: Excise leaf and float on water
steps.instruction: Excise a leaf using surgical scissors (or a hole puncture if necessary) and float it on the surface of water in a petri dish that contains 15 mL water so that subsequent herbicide concentrations can be calculated accurately.

steps.title: Incubate leaves pre‑treatment
steps.instruction: Incubate the excised leaf(s) under the same light conditions described in step 1 for approximately 5 hours.

steps.title: Prepare herbicide solutions
steps.instruction: Add the specified volume of each herbicide stock to 36 mL ethanol to obtain the working solutions:

substeps.instruction: Add 36 µL of 10 mM DBMIB (final concentration = 24 µM).
Add 75 µL of 2 mM DCMU (final concentration = 10 µM).
Add 15 µL of methyl viologen (final concentration = 2.5 µM).
For the control, add 36 µL (or the largest volume used among the herbicides) of ethanol only.

steps.title: Transfer leaves to herbicide solution
steps.instruction: Move the leaf(s) to a new petri dish containing the desired herbicide solution prepared in step 4, or the ethanol control.

steps.title: Vacuum infiltrate leaves
steps.instruction: Place the entire petri dish with leaves into a vacuum chamber and apply the pump for 3 minutes to establish a vacuum; then slowly release the pressure to facilitate uptake of the solution into the leaf tissue.

steps.title: Incubate leaves post‑infiltration
steps.instruction: Incubate the leaves (still immersed in the herbicide solution or control) under the light conditions of step 1 for at least 2 hours.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence and harvest leaves
steps.instruction: Using a PAM fluorometer, record chlorophyll fluorescence parameters (ΦPSII, qP, NPQ) to assess photosynthetic performance; then decide whether to harvest the same leaf or a separate leaf for downstream analyses. If harvesting, snap‑freeze the leaf, grind it, and store the powder at –80 °C. Single leaves of approximately 100 mg are sufficient for mRNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Measure ΦPSII, qP, and NPQ with the PAM.
If required, snap‑freeze the leaf, grind it, and store at –80 °C.
Note that each leaf (~100 mg) serves as one biological replicate, with the petri dish acting as a blocking factor.
